title: Adjunct of the scalar composite mate transported through direct-image compositors
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings, and let $X\xrightarrow rY\xrightarrow sZ$ be arbitrary scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme]. Work in the ordinary unbounded small-etale derived categories $D_R(T)=D(T_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $Q_T=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $P_{u,R}=u_R^*$ for exact constant-ring inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and $R_{u,R}=Ru_{*,R}$, with canonical adjunction $P_{u,R}\dashv R_{u,R}$ and counit $\varepsilon_{u,R}$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Use the normalized isomorphism $\lambda_u:P_{u,B}Q_T\cong Q_WP_{u,A}$ for $u:W\to T$ [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso], and write $\chi_u:Q_TR_{u,A}\to R_{u,B}Q_W$ for its counit-defined mate [def-pur-etale-scalar-mate]. For $M\in D_A(X)$ put $U=R_{r,A}M$, $V=R_{s,A}U$. For any $h:Q_ZV\to R_{s,B}R_{r,B}Q_XM$, define its composite-adjunction adjunct by
$$\operatorname{Adj}_B(h)=\varepsilon_{r,B,Q_XM}\circ P_{r,B}(\varepsilon_{s,B,R_{r,B}Q_XM})\circ P_{r,B}P_{s,B}(h),$$
using the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction].
Let $\kappa_R:R_{sr,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{s,R}R_{r,R}$ be the K-injective-normalized compositor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Put
$$F_M=\kappa_{B,Q_XM}\circ\chi_{sr,M}\circ Q_Z(\kappa_{A,M}^{-1}):Q_ZV\longrightarrow R_{s,B}R_{r,B}Q_XM.$$
Then $\operatorname{Adj}_B(F_M)=T_M$, where
$$T_M=Q_X(\varepsilon_{r,A,M})\circ Q_X(P_{r,A}(\varepsilon_{s,A,U}))\circ\lambda_{r,P_{s,A}V}\circ P_{r,B}(\lambda_{s,V}):P_{r,B}P_{s,B}Q_ZV\longrightarrow Q_XM.$$
The equality uses these specified comparisons and holds without boundedness, properness or coefficient flatness.

proof.text: Write c_R : P_sr,R ≅ P_r,R P_s,R and E_R,N for the composite counit. The existing exact-adjunction specialization of [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization], CategoryTheory.Adjunction.rightDerivedFunctorCompIso'_hom_eq_conjugateEquiv, identifies the actual rightDerivedFunctorCompIso' with the conjugate of c_R. Its ordinary conjugacy premise is congrArg Iso.hom of conjugateIsoEquiv_upperStarComp. Applying conjugateEquiv_counit gives P_sr,R(kappa_R,N inverse);epsilon_sr,R,N = c_R,V;E_R,N. Equivalently epsilon_sr,R,N = c_R,W;P_r,R P_s,R(kappa_R,N);E_R,N by naturality and cancellation. This is exactly the required adjunction compatibility of the specified K-injective and exact-pullback compositors, without constructing the full simultaneous monoidal comparison system.

proof.text:
Put $W=R_{sr,A}M$ and $k=\kappa_{A,M}:W\xrightarrow{\sim}V$. Expand $F_M$ and use Step 1 for $B$. Naturality of $c_B^{-1}$ at $\chi_{sr,M}$, followed by the defining adjunct equation of [def-pur-etale-scalar-mate], gives
$$\operatorname{Adj}_B(F_M)=Q_X(\varepsilon_{sr,A,M})\circ\lambda_{sr,W}\circ c_{B,Q_ZW}^{-1}\circ P_{r,B}P_{s,B}(Q_Z(k^{-1})).$$
Indeed Step 1 replaces $E_B\circ P_{r,B}P_{s,B}(\kappa_B)$ by $\varepsilon_{sr,B}\circ c_B^{-1}$, and the mate definition replaces $\varepsilon_{sr,B}\circ P_{sr,B}(\chi_{sr,M})$ by $Q_X(\varepsilon_{sr,A,M})\circ\lambda_{sr,W}$. Naturality of $c_B^{-1}$ and $\lambda_{sr}$ at $k^{-1}$ now rewrites this as
$$Q_X(\varepsilon_{sr,A,M}\circ P_{sr,A}(k^{-1}))\circ\lambda_{sr,V}\circ c_{B,Q_ZV}^{-1}.$$ In Lean, first transport the defining mate counit equation along leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory using mapDerivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction_eq. Naturality of the inverse comparison and cancellation of the A comparison with its inverse give the exact-pullback counit equation.

proof.text:
Specialize [lem-sf-scalar-pullback-composition] to $j_1=r$, $v=s$, $j_2=sr$, and $N=V$. Its comparisons are precisely these $c_R$: both are the canonical module inverse-image compositors, transported to the derived categories, with the ordinary composition normalization on K-flat representatives. Its $\lambda$ is the specified scalarPullbackIso. It states
$$Q_X(c_{A,V})\circ\lambda_{sr,V}=\lambda_{r,P_{s,A}V}\circ P_{r,B}(\lambda_{s,V})\circ c_{B,Q_ZV}.$$
Set $L=\lambda_{r,P_{s,A}V}\circ P_{r,B}(\lambda_{s,V})$. Cancel the two composition isomorphisms and substitute into Step 2 to obtain
$$\operatorname{Adj}_B(F_M)=Q_X(\varepsilon_{sr,A,M}\circ P_{sr,A}(k^{-1})\circ c_{A,V}^{-1})\circ L.$$

source.place: Tag 0E46, remark-compose-base-change (omitted verification), using Tags 07A7, 0D6D and 0D6E

proof.text:
Naturality of $c_A$ at $k^{-1}:V\to W$ gives
$$c_{A,W}\circ P_{sr,A}(k^{-1})\circ c_{A,V}^{-1}=P_{r,A}P_{s,A}(k^{-1}).$$
Insert the Step-1 formula for $\varepsilon_{sr,A,M}$. The factor $P_{r,A}P_{s,A}(k)$ cancels $P_{r,A}P_{s,A}(k^{-1})$, so the parenthesized map in Step 3 equals $E_{A,M}$. Therefore $\operatorname{Adj}_B(F_M)=Q_X(E_{A,M})\circ L=T_M$ by functoriality of $Q_X$ and the displayed definitions of $E$ and $L$. Only $k,c_A,c_B$ were inverted; no $\chi$ was inverted and no boundedness or flatness was used.
